Execute step A2 of the build plan at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` — read that file's A2 section (search for `### A2 — Add the`) in full; this prompt summarises the decisions but the plan file is authoritative if anything here is ambiguous.

## Files to touch (only these three)

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`

**Do not touch `zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`** (the recipe file) — this is an explicit constraint already stated elsewhere in the plan: if satisfying this step seems to require a recipe change, stop and report that rather than making one. Everything below is achievable with plain Chakra props on the render body alone.

## Read these two files fully before writing anything

Both already exist and you are NOT modifying them — read them to understand exactly what you're composing and what patterns already exist:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` — the `ZimmProductCardMedia` molecule this organism composes.
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` — the `ZimmProductCardContent` molecule, in particular its `ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink)` pattern (imports `Link as RouteLink` from `react-router-dom`) — mirror this exact import/wrap idiom in `index.tsx`, don't invent a different one.

## What to change in `index.tsx`

**1. Add the new variation type** (no additions — matches `ZimmProductCardHomeVariation`'s own "no additions" shape exactly):
```ts
export type ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation = {
  variation: 'recentlyViewed';
  // No additions — the rail tile is image-only; see VARIATION_CONFIG and the module docblock.
};
```
Add it to the `ZimmProductCardProps` union and to the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union (both currently list `plp | home | wishlist` — add `recentlyViewed` as the fourth member of each, sourced the same way the other three are: `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation['variation']`).

**2. Add `showContent: boolean` to `ZimmProductCardVariationConfig`**, with a JSDoc comment in the same style as every other field in that type (e.g. explain it exists to let `recentlyViewed` suppress `ZimmProductCardContent` wholesale, unlike every other flag in this type which only ever hides a *sub-part* of Content).

**3. Add `showContent: true` to the existing `home`, `plp`, and `wishlist` rows** in `VARIATION_CONFIG` (the type gains a required field, so all three existing rows need it — they've shown full content since day one, this is just making that explicit).

**4. Add the `recentlyViewed` row to `VARIATION_CONFIG`** — every flag `false`:
```ts
recentlyViewed: {
  showBag: false,
  showAttributes: false,
  showSizeChips: false,
  hoverHidesPrice: false,
  hoverRevealsPrice: false,
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
  showRemove: false,
  // Moot — there is no bag on any viewport for this variation (Card-content is hidden
  // wholesale below), so this flag never actually applies. Figma nodes: Desktop 40000307:12444,
  // Tablet 40000730:13363, Mobile 40000538:25030 — Card-content `hidden="true"` on all three.
  hideBagOnMobile: false,
  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
  showBadge: false,
  showHoverImageSwap: false,
  showContent: false,
},
```

**5. Change the render body's return statement.** Currently it unconditionally renders `ZimmProductCardMedia` then `ZimmProductCardContent` as two siblings inside the root `chakra.div`. Change this to a conditional:

- **When `config.showContent` is true** (home/plp/wishlist): render exactly what's there today — `ZimmProductCardMedia` (with `onClick={handleMediaClick}`, unchanged) followed by `ZimmProductCardContent` (unchanged), wrapped in a `<>...</>` fragment since these are two siblings.
- **When `config.showContent` is false** (`recentlyViewed` only): render a `react-router-dom` `Link` (via `chakra(RouteLink)`, same import/wrap pattern as `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `ProductNameLink` — add this as a new local `const` near the top of `index.tsx`, not inline) with `to={href}` and `display="block"` (a plain Chakra prop, not `sx` — this is needed because an anchor is inline by default and it's wrapping a block-level `ZimmProductCardMedia`). Inside that Link: Chakra's own `VisuallyHidden` (import it from `@chakra-ui/react` alongside the other Chakra imports already at the top of the file) wrapping `{name}` as real, visually-hidden text — this is the link's accessible name, since nothing else in this branch is visible. Then `ZimmProductCardMedia`, with **no `onClick` prop at all** (the real `Link` handles navigation and keyboard operability natively — `handleMediaClick`'s click-passthrough workaround exists only to route around the other three variations' invisible stretched-overlay anchor, which doesn't exist in this branch since the `Link` directly contains the image instead of sitting behind it as an overlay).

  For this branch's `ZimmProductCardMedia` call: `primaryImage`/`hoverImage`/`images` pass through as normal; `swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}` (same expression as the other branch — it already resolves to `false` here since `config.showHoverImageSwap` is `false`, so reuse it rather than hardcoding a special-cased `false` literal); `showControls` can stay `true` (moot — single image means no arrows regardless); `badge={resolvedBadge}` is fine to include (already resolves to `undefined` since `config.showBadge` is `false`); do **not** pass `onRemove`/`removeLabel` (both are already `undefined` for this variation via the existing derivations, but there's nothing to plumb through in this branch's own JSX either way).

## Docblock updates (still in `index.tsx`)

**A.** The module docblock currently has this paragraph (search for `Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to`):
> "...Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it."

Rewrite this as a **record of what was done**, not an instruction to a future builder — state that a dedicated `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry was added (citing Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236 as the source for the badge/hover-swap suppression), and add the note about editorial/landing pages remaining unscoped (comment 13880 also asks for the same suppression there, but that surface has no ticket/design/AC today — a future variation for it must **not** reuse `recentlyViewed`, since the name would misdescribe it, and must not use `plp` either).

**B.** Add a new paragraph to the variation-matrix part of the docblock (alongside the existing Home/PLP/Wishlist paragraphs) describing `recentlyViewed`: image-only, every flag off, no name/price/bag/attributes/badge — and briefly why a real (but hidden) link still exists: `ZimmProductCardContent` is unmounted entirely for this variation, but its own name-link is this card's only keyboard-reachable element, so a minimal `Link` + `VisuallyHidden`-wrapped name is composed directly in this file instead, confined to this file only (no changes to `ZimmProductCardContent`/`ZimmProductCardMedia`). Cite SFCC-83 AC 4 (tile click navigates to PDP) as the requirement this satisfies.

## Tests (`index.test.tsx`)

- Add a `buildCardProps` overload for `'recentlyViewed'` (matching the existing overloaded pattern for `'plp'`/`'home'`/`'wishlist'`) — no extra fields beyond the base ones, matching `'home'`'s own case.
- `@ts-expect-error` cases: assigning `colour`/`size`/`onRemove` (or any PLP/Wishlist-only field) to `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` must fail to compile — same pattern as the existing `home` case in the "discriminated union is enforced at compile time" describe block, assigned to the **narrow intersection type**, not the `ZimmProductCardProps` union alias.
- Badge suppression test: pass `badge="Runway"` to a `recentlyViewed` card, assert no `[data-card-slot="badge"]` (or equivalent) renders. **Make it fail on purpose first**: temporarily flip `showBadge: true` in your own local edit, confirm the test fails, then flip it back to `false` before finishing.
- Hover-swap suppression test: same shape, with `hoverImage` supplied, asserting no `[data-role="hover-overlay"]` mounts. Same fail-first requirement.
- `ZimmProductCardContent` absence test: render a `recentlyViewed` card (with `currentPrice` and other Content-relevant props supplied, to prove they're genuinely suppressed, not just never passed), assert `document.querySelector('[data-card-slot="content"]')` is null.
- Real-link test: assert `screen.getByRole('link', {name: <the product name used in the fixture>})` finds exactly one link, and that this is the *only* link on a `recentlyViewed` card (reuse the existing "exactly one real anchor regardless of variation" describe block's pattern — add `recentlyViewed` to its `test.each` array, or add a dedicated test if the existing one can't cleanly extend to assert the link's accessible name specifically).
- Confirm `ZimmProductCardMedia` receives no `onClick` for `recentlyViewed` — you can assert this behaviourally: clicking the image directly should NOT call any click-passthrough handler (there is none in this branch), only the real `Link`'s native navigation applies. If there's no clean way to assert "no onClick was wired" directly, it's acceptable to skip a dedicated test for this and just confirm via code review that the JSX omits it — say so in your report rather than forcing an awkward test.
- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` must still return zero hits after your change.

## Story (`index.stories.tsx`)

Add a `RecentlyViewed` named export, following the existing story pattern (`Default`, `Home`, `Wishlist`, etc.) — single primary image only (no `hoverImage`, no `images`, no `badge`, no `onAddToBag`/`onRemove`/size chips — none of those apply to this variation and passing them would misleadingly imply they do something). Docblock comment should note this variation renders image-only per Figma (cite the same node IDs as the `hideBagOnMobile` comment above: Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030`) and that the product name is present as visually-hidden accessible text on the wrapping link, not visible on screen — a reviewer eyeballing this story should not expect to see the name and should confirm via the accessibility tree / tab order instead.

## Pass criteria (verify all before reporting)

- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, including the new `@ts-expect-error` cases resolving as genuinely used (not "unused directive" errors).
- `npm run test` green, including `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (should be unaffected since you're not touching the recipe, but confirm).
- `npm run lint` — compare your own count against a fresh baseline you check first; do not introduce new problems.
- Both new fail-first tests (badge, hover-swap) were genuinely proven to fail when you temporarily flipped the flag, before you flipped it back — say so explicitly in your report, the same way A1's rework round did.

## Scope boundary

Only the three files named above. Do not touch `zimmProductCard.css.ts`, `zimmProductCardContent/*`, or `zimmProductCardMedia/*` — if you find yourself needing to, stop and report why rather than proceeding. Do not stage or commit — the orchestrating skill handles that after review.

When done, report: a summary of the exact diff shape, confirmation of every pass criterion above with real command output (not just "should pass"), and anything you found ambiguous or had to make a judgment call on.

1	# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan
2	
3	**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
4	**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)
5	
6	## 1. Goal statement
7	
8	Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
9	`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
10	(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
11	corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
12	**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
13	(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
14	**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
15	card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
16	recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
17	
18	Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
19	**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
20	bodies; must not reach production.
21	
22	## 2. Scale call
23	
24	### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port
25	
26	Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
27	`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
28	file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
29	true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
30	overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.
31	
32	Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
33	`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
34	— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
35	Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
36	redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.
37	
38	**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
39	required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
40	direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
41	dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
42	the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
43	`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
44	(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
45	resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.
46	
47	**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
48	only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
49	So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
50	running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.
51	
52	Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
53	five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:
54	
55	| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
58	| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
59	| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
60	| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |
61	
62	It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
63	`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
64	`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
65	render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.
66	
67	**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
68	`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
69	table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
70	but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
71	*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
72	`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
73	itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
74	issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
75	(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
76	of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
77	Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
78	after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).
79	
80	**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
81	Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
82	silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
83	E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
84	2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
85	package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
86	`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
87	new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
88	A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
89	in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.
90	
91	Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
92	but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
93	Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
94	presence on PLP as scope creep.

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
bodies; must not reach production.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by

### A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.

This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside
  the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. One import, one call, guarded by the same
  `if (product)`.
- `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.

**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
rather than assumed.

**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never
viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by Open Question 6. Do not
paper over it with a heuristic.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `false`, resolved in `useEffect`. No `sessionStorage` access during render.
  No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on first paint and appears after hydration. (Also
  good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on `sessionStorage`. Failure degrades to `false`
  (no rail), never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`;
  `sessionStorage` throwing → `false`; first render before effect → `false`.

   SFCC-236's **Variation extensibility** AC makes adding a fifth row later a one-entry change.
   **Consequence to carry forward:** when editorial/landing pages *are* scoped, they need their own
   `VARIATION_CONFIG` row with `showBadge: false` + `showHoverImageSwap: false` — they must **not**
   reuse `recentlyViewed`, and must not use `plp` (which would ship the badge Dani ruled out). Record
   this in A2's docblock update so the next reader finds it.

10. **🔴 NEW — PRD §7.5 vs the design (finding 37).** §7.5 (SPR-62, *Confirmed*) promises Add to Bag
    from recommendation carousels on PDP and Cart; the rail's design has neither bag nor size
    selector. **Adjudicated by Marcel 2026-09-06: design wins**, on the grounds that §7.5's own note
    defers the Add-to-Bag-vs-Wishlist choice and Recently Viewed is §7.4. Built accordingly, but the
    PR body must state the divergence — it is a live confirmed-PRD conflict, not a closed one.
    **Owner: Jasmijn / Dani to ratify.**

11. **🔵 An unresolvable node in the supplied set (finding 40).** `9086:9335` in `Zimmermann_Designs`
    returns "node may have been deleted, or the ID was extracted incorrectly" — same class as the
    earlier `8802:10232`. Its `9086:*` siblings in the supplied list are unverified. Nothing in the
    plan depends on them. **Owner: Marcel, only if those nodes were meant to carry something.**

12. ~~**PDP's `RecommendedProducts` import never redirects to our override.**~~ **CLOSED — folded
    into A6 (Marcel, 2026-09-06).** Discovered during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification: PDP
    showed zero marker fires even on a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and
    repeatedly. Verified directly against `overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source (not just this
    plan's earlier paraphrase of it): `isFromExtends` returns `false` whenever the issuing file is
    itself inside `overrides/`, and `product-detail/index.tsx` is such a file — so its
    package-path import of `RecommendedProducts` was never going to redirect to our new override,
    regardless of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data (all three were investigated and
    ruled out first). As originally planned this meant PDP's Recently Viewed rail would never
    render even after A6 landed the branch — a real architectural gap, not a testing quirk, and
    one no test would have caught (no PR-time E2E on this path). Fix: change
    `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s import from base package path to relative, the same
    `overrideStyling.md` "Importing an already-overridden component" doctrine A6 already applies
    to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself in the original
    draft. See the correction in §2 "Architecture fork" and A6's updated step and pass criteria.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
5	import { ZimmProductName } from '../../atoms/zimmProductName';
6	import { ZimmProductPrice } from '../../atoms/zimmProductPrice';
7	import { ZimmIcon } from '../../atoms/zimmIcon';
8	import { ZimmSizeChipGroup } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	import { CARD_SLOT } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';
11	
12	/**
13	 * Selector contract for a later step (the ZimmProductCard organism, SFCC-236 Step 6): stable
14	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target
15	 * these descendants for hover-reveal styling without reaching into implementation details.
16	 * Do not rename these values without updating that recipe too — mirrors the same contract
17	 * `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` documents for its own slots:
18	 *   - "content"   — the outermost element (this component's root).
19	 *   - "price"     — the price wrapper. Always rendered regardless of variation; the organism's
20	 *                   own CSS is what shows/hides it on hover per variation (see the `showBag`/
21	 *                   `showSizeChips` props below), not this component.
22	 *   - "sizeChips" — the size-chip-group wrapper (present only when `showSizeChips` is true).
23	 *                   Always rendered in the DOM per Figma's `hidden=true` default on the "Size
24	 *                   Selector instance" node — the organism's hover-reveal CSS is what handles
25	 *                   visibility, not this component's own recipe (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts).
26	 *   - "bag"       — the bag-button wrapper (present only when `showBag` is true). Added later
27	 *                   than the three above, for the organism's own mobile-breakpoint hide rule
28	 *                   (Figma: PLP/PDP's Mobile Card-content instances have the bag icon's `Icons`
29	 *                   frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop and Wishlist's own Mobile instance do not) — a
30	 *                   viewport-width concern, not a hover one, but the same
31	 *                   "this component always renders it, the organism's CSS decides visibility"
32	 *                   division of responsibility as the other slots.
33	 */
34	
35	// Same import base SFCC's own swatch-group/swatch.jsx uses for its `RouteLink`, and the same
36	// reasoning zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx already documents: a router `Link` delivers "URL updates
37	// without a full page reload" for real. Confirmed directly (no overrides/app/components/link/
38	// directory exists on disk) — there is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse instead.
39	const ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink);
40	
41	const messages = defineMessages({
42	  // Deliberately generic, not name-interpolated ("Add {name} to bag") — no such requirement was
43	  // given, and the visible product name already sits immediately to this button's left in the
44	  // same row, so the accessible name does not need to repeat it.
45	  addToBag: { id: 'product_card_content.bag.add_to_bag', defaultMessage: 'Add to bag' },
46	  // Figma node 40002163:41468 (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True) — an instance of the
47	  // shared CTA/Link atom (40001908:28374/40001908:28368) with its text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in
48	  // this state. Authored here in sentence case, not literal caps, matching this codebase's
49	  // pattern of keeping translatable copy normal-case and letting the textStyle's CSS apply the
50	  // visual transform (see ZimmProductName's own normal-cased stories against `productNames`'
51	  // textTransform: 'uppercase') — `linkSm` was corrected to `textTransform: 'uppercase'` to
52	  // match (2026-09-03, theme/foundation/typography.ts), so this renders "NOTIFY ME" correctly.
53	  notifyMe: {
54	    id: 'product_card_content.notify_me.label',
55	    defaultMessage: 'Notify me',
56	  },
57	});
58	
59	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCardContent';
60	
61	/**
62	 * `ZimmProductName`'s own heading-level prop, read off the atom's real signature via a utility
63	 * type rather than a hand-typed duplicate union (typescript.md: "prefer utility types over
64	 * hand-rolled duplicate shapes... a hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
65	 * original changes"). Its type param is `'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` — note this is NOT `'h2' | 'h3' |
66	 * 'h4'` as an earlier sketch of this component's contract assumed; see `headingLevel` below.
67	 */
68	type ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductName>['as'];
69	
70	export type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
71	  /** The product's display name, rendered as the card's heading and link text. */
72	  name: string;
73	  /**
74	   * Heading level for the composed `ZimmProductName`, forwarded to it as `as`. Named
75	   * `headingLevel` here (rather than `as`) because this component is not itself polymorphic —
76	   * it always renders the same fixed element tree, it just hands the one real heading a level.
77	   * Typed as `ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel` (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`) to exactly match what that atom
78	   * actually accepts — a prior sketch of this contract assumed `'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'`, which is
79	   * wrong on both ends: the atom has no `'h4'` at all, and it does accept `'h1'` (unlikely in
80	   * practice for a grid card, but not this component's place to forbid what the atom allows).
81	   */
82	  headingLevel: ZimmProductNameHeadingLevel;
83	  /**
84	   * PDP destination for the product name link. Not passed through `isSafeHref` — unlike
85	   * `ZimmNavItem`/`ZimmContactIconRow`'s CMS-sourced hrefs, this is an SFCC-generated product URL,
86	   * the same trust level `ZimmColourSwatch`'s own `href` prop already assumes.
87	   */
88	  href: string;
89	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
90	  currentPrice?: string;
91	  /** Passed straight through to the composed `ZimmProductPrice`. */
92	  originalPrice?: string;
93	  /** Passed straight through to `ZimmProductPrice`'s own `isLoading`. */
94	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
95	
96	  /**
97	   * Wishlist-only attributes line (colour + size as plain text), per the organism's
98	   * VARIATION_CONFIG (Step 6, not built yet) — this component only ever sees the resolved
99	   * boolean, never a variation name. When false the row is absent from the DOM entirely, not
100	   * merely visually hidden.
101	   */
102	  showAttributes: boolean;
103	  /**
104	   * Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. Pass the plain colour value ("Ivory", not
105	   * "Ivory,") — the component itself appends the trailing comma when rendering, matching
106	   * Figma's own text-node structure (confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446:
107	   * the colour text node's own content literally includes the trailing comma, e.g. "Lilac
108	   * Sand,", not a separate punctuation node). See the `colourWithComma` derivation below.
109	   */
110	  colour?: string;
111	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
112	  size?: string;
113	
114	  /** Renders the bag button (Figma "Icon_bag" — confirmed a bag action, not a wishlist star). */
115	  showBag: boolean;
116	  /** Disables the bag button (native `disabled`) when true. `onAddToBag` never fires in that state. */
117	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
118	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
119	
120	  /**
121	   * PLP-only size-chip picker, per the organism's config. Always rendered in the DOM whenever
122	   * true — Figma's `hidden=true` default on this slot is a hover-reveal CSS concern for the
123	   * Step 6 organism, not something this component enforces on itself. See the module docblock's
124	   * `data-card-slot="sizeChips"` note.
125	   */
126	  showSizeChips: boolean;
127	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
128	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
129	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
130	
131	  /**
132	   * True only when the caller has already resolved "unavailable AND a usable notify-me callback
133	   * exists" (the organism's job). This component still independently requires `onNotifyMe` to be
134	   * present before rendering anything — belt-and-braces, the same defensive shape
135	   * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onRemove` + `removeLabel` co-requirement uses.
136	   */
137	  showNotifyMe: boolean;
138	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
139	};
140	
141	/**
142	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
143	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
144	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
145	 * 40002163:37103).
146	 *
147	 * Deliberately has NO remove/close button — that action lives entirely in
148	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not here.
149	 *
150	 * Also deliberately has no badge slot, despite the SFCC-236 AC mentioning one for PLP/Wishlist.
151	 * An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed no Figma design existed for it at all — that
152	 * was wrong: the badge (Figma "Tag") does exist, confirmed present and identical across every
153	 * Size/Type variant checked. It just lives inside "Image Group", which is
154	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain, not this component's — so it was built there instead. See
155	 * that component's own docblock for the confirmed spec, and the organism's own docblock
156	 * ("Badge" note) for which variations actually show it.
157	 *
158	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
159	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
160	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
161	 */
162	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
163	  name,
164	  headingLevel,
165	  href,
166	  currentPrice,
167	  originalPrice,
168	  isPriceLoading,
169	  showAttributes,
170	  colour,
171	  size,
172	  showBag,
173	  isUnavailable,
174	  onAddToBag,
175	  showSizeChips,
176	  sizeChipValues,
177	  selectedSizeChipValue,
178	  onSizeChipSelect,
179	  showNotifyMe,
180	  onNotifyMe,
181	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
182	  const intl = useIntl();
183	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
184	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
185	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
186	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
187	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
188	
189	  // Both conditions required, matching the component contract exactly — not just `showNotifyMe`
190	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
191	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
192	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
193	
194	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
195	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
196	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
197	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
198	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
199	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
200	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
201	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
202	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
203	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
204	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
205	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
206	
207	  return (
208	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.content}>
209	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
210	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
211	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
212	        </ProductNameLink>
213	
214	        {showBag && (
215	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.bag}>
216	            <chakra.button
217	              type="button"
218	              __css={styles.bagButton}
219	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
220	              disabled={isUnavailable}
221	              onClick={() => {
222	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
223	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
224	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
225	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
226	                if (isUnavailable) return;
227	                onAddToBag?.();
228	              }}
229	            >
230	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
231	            </chakra.button>
232	          </chakra.div>
233	        )}
234	      </chakra.div>
235	
236	      {showAttributes && (
237	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
238	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
239	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
240	        </chakra.div>
241	      )}
242	
243	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.price}>
244	        <ZimmProductPrice
245	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
246	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
247	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
248	          isLive={false}
249	        />
250	      </chakra.div>
251	
252	      {showSizeChips && (
253	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}>
254	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
255	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
256	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
257	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
258	          />
259	        </chakra.div>
260	      )}
261	
262	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
263	        <chakra.button
264	          type="button"
265	          __css={styles.notifyMeButton}
266	          onClick={onNotifyMe}
267	          data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}
268	        >
269	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
270	        </chakra.button>
271	      )}
272	    </chakra.div>
273	  );
274	};
275	
276	export default ZimmProductCardContent;

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { useHistory } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
5	import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
6	import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
7	import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
8	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
9	
10	/**
11	 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
12	 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
13	 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
14	 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
15	 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
16	 *
17	 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
18	 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
19	 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
20	 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
21	 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
22	 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
23	 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
24	 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
25	 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
26	 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
27	 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
28	 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
29	 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
30	 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
31	 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
32	 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
33	 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
34	 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
35	 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
36	 *
37	 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
38	 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
39	 *
40	 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
41	 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
42	 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
43	 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
44	 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
45	 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
46	 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
47	 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
48	 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
49	 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
50	 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
51	 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
52	 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
53	 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
54	 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
55	 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
56	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
57	 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
58	 *
59	 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
60	 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
61	 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
62	 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
63	 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
64	 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
65	 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
66	 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
67	 *
68	 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
69	 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
70	 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
71	 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
72	 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
73	 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
74	 *     leaves it visible.
75	 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
76	 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
77	 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
78	 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
79	 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
80	 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
81	 *     which of the two reasons applies.
82	 *
83	 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
84	 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
85	 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
86	 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
87	 *
88	 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
89	 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
90	 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
91	 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
92	 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
93	 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
94	 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
95	 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
96	 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
97	 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
98	 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
99	 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
100	 * rather than silently picked.
101	 *
102	 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
103	 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
104	 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
105	 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
106	 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
107	 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
108	 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
109	 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
110	 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
111	 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
112	 *
113	 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
114	 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
115	 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
116	 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
117	 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
118	 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
119	 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
120	 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
121	 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
122	 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
123	 *
124	 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
125	 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
126	 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
127	 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
128	 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
129	 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
130	 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
131	 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
132	 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
133	 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
134	 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
135	 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
136	 *
137	 * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
138	 * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
139	 * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
140	 * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
141	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
142	 * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
143	 * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
144	 * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
145	 * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
146	 * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
147	 * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
148	 * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
149	 * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
150	 * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
151	 * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
152	 * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
153	 * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
154	 * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
155	 * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
156	 * so paging and `onRemove` keep firing on their own and never also navigate. No custom drag-vs-tap
157	 * detection is needed for the swipe/tap split itself: browsers natively suppress the synthetic
158	 * `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe pages the gallery without
159	 * ever reaching this handler, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires it exactly as the old
160	 * overlay click did.
161	 */
162	
163	/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
164	 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
165	 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
166	export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;
167	
168	/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
169	 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
170	 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
171	type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];
172	
173	/**
174	 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
175	 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
176	 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
177	 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
178	 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
179	 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
180	 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
181	 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
182	 * `buildCardProps` helper.
183	 */
184	export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
185	  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
186	   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
187	   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
188	   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
189	  id: string;
190	  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
191	   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
192	  href: string;
193	  name: string;
194	  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
195	  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
196	  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
197	  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
198	  currentPrice?: string;
199	  originalPrice?: string;
200	  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
201	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
202	  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
203	   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
204	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
205	  /**
206	   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
207	   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
208	   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
209	   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
210	   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
211	   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
212	   */
213	  badge?: string;
214	};
215	
216	export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
217	  variation: 'plp';
218	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
219	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
220	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
221	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
222	};
223	
224	export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
225	  variation: 'home';
226	  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
227	};
228	
229	export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
230	  variation: 'wishlist';
231	  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
232	  colour: string;
233	  size: string;
234	  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
235	  onRemove: () => void;
236	  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
237	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
238	  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
239	   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
240	   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
241	   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
242	   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
243	   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
244	   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
245	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
246	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
247	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
248	};
249	
250	export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
251	  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);
252	
253	type ZimmProductCardVariation =
254	  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
255	  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
256	  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];
257	
258	/**
259	 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
260	 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
261	 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
262	 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
263	 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
264	 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
265	 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
266	 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
267	 */
268	type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
269	  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
270	    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
271	    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
272	>;
273	
274	type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
275	  showBag: boolean;
276	  showAttributes: boolean;
277	  showSizeChips: boolean;
278	  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
279	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
280	  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
281	  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
282	  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
283	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
284	  showRemove: boolean;
285	  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
286	   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
287	   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
288	   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
289	  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
290	  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
291	   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
292	   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
293	   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
294	   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
295	   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
296	   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
297	  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
298	  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
299	  showBadge: boolean;
300	  /**
301	   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
302	   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
303	   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
304	   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
305	   */
306	  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
307	};
308	
309	/**
310	 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
311	 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
312	 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
313	 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
314	 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
315	 */
316	const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
317	  home: {
318	    showBag: false,
319	    showAttributes: false,
320	    showSizeChips: false,
321	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
322	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
323	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
324	    showRemove: false,
325	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
326	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
327	    showBadge: false,
328	    showHoverImageSwap: false,
329	  },
330	  plp: {
331	    showBag: true,
332	    showAttributes: false,
333	    showSizeChips: true,
334	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
335	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
336	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
337	    showRemove: false,
338	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
339	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
340	    showBadge: true,
341	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
342	  },
343	  wishlist: {
344	    showBag: true,
345	    showAttributes: true,
346	    showSizeChips: true,
347	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
348	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
349	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
350	    showRemove: true,
351	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
352	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
353	    showBadge: true,
354	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
355	  },
356	};
357	
358	const messages = defineMessages({
359	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
360	  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
361	  // site that actually knows the product name.
362	  removeFromWishlist: {
363	    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
364	    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
365	  },
366	});
367	
368	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';
369	
370	/**
371	 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
372	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
373	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
374	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
375	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
376	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
377	 *
378	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
379	 */
380	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
381	  const {
382	    id,
383	    href,
384	    name,
385	    headingLevel,
386	    primaryImage,
387	    hoverImage,
388	    images,
389	    currentPrice,
390	    originalPrice,
391	    isPriceLoading,
392	    isUnavailable,
393	    onNotifyMe,
394	    badge,
395	    variation,
396	  } = props;
397	
398	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
399	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
400	
401	  const intl = useIntl();
402	  const history = useHistory();
403	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
404	
405	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
406	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
407	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
408	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
409	
410	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
411	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
412	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
413	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
414	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
415	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
416	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
417	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
418	  //
419	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
420	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
421	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
422	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
423	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
424	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
425	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
426	  //
427	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
428	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
429	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
430	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
431	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
432	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
433	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
434	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
435	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
436	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
437	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
438	
439	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
440	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
441	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
442	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
443	  // not why.
444	  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
445	
446	  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
447	  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
448	
449	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
450	    hoverHidesPrice,
451	    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
452	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
453	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
454	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
455	    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
456	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
457	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
458	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
459	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
460	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
461	    // mounted at all.
462	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
463	    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
464	  });
465	
466	  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
467	  // two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real <button> descendants of
468	  // ZimmProductCardMedia) so paging/onRemove keep firing on their own and never also navigate.
469	  // Fix L (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a real <a> lets the
470	  // browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button
471	  // clicks natively — this handler only ever replaces the in-page navigation an UNMODIFIED,
472	  // primary-button click used to reach via the stretched-link overlay (see Fix I). Bailing out on
473	  // any of those instead of forcing an in-tab `history.push` regardless of what the shopper
474	  // actually asked for; a no-op here is a real gap (it doesn't open a new tab the way a real link
475	  // would) but is strictly better than silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal.
476	  const handleMediaClick = (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>): void => {
477	    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
478	    if (target.closest('button')) return;
479	    if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey || event.button !== 0) return;
480	    history.push(href);
481	  };
482	
483	  return (
484	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
485	      <ZimmProductCardMedia
486	        primaryImage={primaryImage}
487	        hoverImage={hoverImage}
488	        images={images}
489	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
490	        showControls
491	        badge={resolvedBadge}
492	        onRemove={onRemove}
493	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
494	        onClick={handleMediaClick}
495	      />
496	      <ZimmProductCardContent
497	        name={name}
498	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
499	        href={href}
500	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
501	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
502	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
503	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
504	        colour={colour}
505	        size={size}
506	        showBag={config.showBag}
507	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
508	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
509	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
510	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
511	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
512	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
513	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
514	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
515	      />
516	    </chakra.div>
517	  );
518	};
519	
520	export default ZimmProductCard;
521
