import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { useHistory } from 'react-router-dom';
import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';

/**
 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
 *
 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
 *
 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
 *
 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
 *     leaves it visible.
 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
 *     which of the two reasons applies.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
 *
 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
 * rather than silently picked.
 *
 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
 *
 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
 *
 * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
 * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
 * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
 * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
 * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
 * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
 * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
 * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
 * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
 * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
 * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
 * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
 * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
 * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
 * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
 * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
 * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
 * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
 * so paging and `onRemove` keep firing on their own and never also navigate. No custom drag-vs-tap
 * detection is needed for the swipe/tap split itself: browsers natively suppress the synthetic
 * `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe pages the gallery without
 * ever reaching this handler, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires it exactly as the old
 * overlay click did.
 */

/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;

/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];

/**
 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
 * `buildCardProps` helper.
 */
export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
  id: string;
  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
  href: string;
  name: string;
  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
  currentPrice?: string;
  originalPrice?: string;
  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
  isUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
  /**
   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
   */
  badge?: string;
};

export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
  variation: 'plp';
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
  variation: 'home';
  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
};

export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
  variation: 'wishlist';
  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
  colour: string;
  size: string;
  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
  onRemove: () => void;
  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);

type ZimmProductCardVariation =
  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];

/**
 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
 */
type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
>;

type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
  showBag: boolean;
  showAttributes: boolean;
  showSizeChips: boolean;
  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
  showRemove: boolean;
  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
  showBadge: boolean;
  /**
   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
   */
  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
};

/**
 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
 */
const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
  home: {
    showBag: false,
    showAttributes: false,
    showSizeChips: false,
    hoverHidesPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
    showRemove: false,
    hideBagOnMobile: false,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
    showBadge: false,
    showHoverImageSwap: false,
  },
  plp: {
    showBag: true,
    showAttributes: false,
    showSizeChips: true,
    hoverHidesPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
    showRemove: false,
    hideBagOnMobile: true,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
    showBadge: true,
    showHoverImageSwap: true,
  },
  wishlist: {
    showBag: true,
    showAttributes: true,
    showSizeChips: true,
    hoverHidesPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
    showRemove: true,
    hideBagOnMobile: false,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
    showBadge: true,
    showHoverImageSwap: true,
  },
};

const messages = defineMessages({
  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
  // site that actually knows the product name.
  removeFromWishlist: {
    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
  },
});

const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';

/**
 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
 *
 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
 */
export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
  const {
    id,
    href,
    name,
    headingLevel,
    primaryImage,
    hoverImage,
    images,
    currentPrice,
    originalPrice,
    isPriceLoading,
    isUnavailable,
    onNotifyMe,
    badge,
    variation,
  } = props;

  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;

  const intl = useIntl();
  const history = useHistory();
  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];

  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);

  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
  //
  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
  //
  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);

  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
  // not why.
  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));

  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;

  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
    hoverHidesPrice,
    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
    // mounted at all.
    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
  });

  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
  // two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real <button> descendants of
  // ZimmProductCardMedia) so paging/onRemove keep firing on their own and never also navigate.
  // Fix L (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a real <a> lets the
  // browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button
  // clicks natively — this handler only ever replaces the in-page navigation an UNMODIFIED,
  // primary-button click used to reach via the stretched-link overlay (see Fix I). Bailing out on
  // any of those instead of forcing an in-tab `history.push` regardless of what the shopper
  // actually asked for; a no-op here is a real gap (it doesn't open a new tab the way a real link
  // would) but is strictly better than silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal.
  const handleMediaClick = (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>): void => {
    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
    if (target.closest('button')) return;
    if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey || event.button !== 0) return;
    history.push(href);
  };

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
      <ZimmProductCardMedia
        primaryImage={primaryImage}
        hoverImage={hoverImage}
        images={images}
        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
        showControls
        badge={resolvedBadge}
        onRemove={onRemove}
        removeLabel={removeLabel}
        onClick={handleMediaClick}
      />
      <ZimmProductCardContent
        name={name}
        headingLevel={headingLevel}
        href={href}
        currentPrice={currentPrice}
        originalPrice={originalPrice}
        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
        colour={colour}
        size={size}
        showBag={config.showBag}
        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
      />
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

export default ZimmProductCard;

343	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].

345	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
346	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
347	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
348	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
349	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
350	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
351	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
352	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
353	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
354	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: {
355	        zIndex: 1,
356	      },
357	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
358	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in

360	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
361	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
362	        zIndex: 1,
363	      },
364	      // Fix J — belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6's own Fix J note): the carousel wrapper's
365	      // arrow buttons carry their own `pointerEvents: 'auto'` unconditionally
366	      // (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `arrowButton` part) — harmless while the wrapper was
367	      // `display: 'none'` by default (that alone removed the whole subtree from hit-testing), but
368	      // no longer guaranteed once the wrapper's hidden state is `clipPath`-based instead (below,
369	      // and in `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `carousel` part). Re-enabled only inside the
370	      // same two revealed selectors, alongside the existing carousel reveal further below.
371	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
372	        pointerEvents: 'none',
373	      },
374	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
375	        position: 'relative',
376	        zIndex: 1,
377	      },
378	      // Fix I — the media/gallery scroll region itself, lifted the same way `close`/`carousel`
379	      // already are (docblock point 2's new bullet has the full narrative). `zIndex` is all
380	      // that's needed: ZimmProductCardMedia's own root recipe already sets `position: 'relative'`.
381	      // `cursor: 'pointer'` is added alongside it — this element is no longer inside the overlay
382	      // `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor, and
383	      // index.tsx's own new `onClick` (see that file's docblock) makes it genuinely clickable
384	      // again.
385	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: {
386	        zIndex: 1,
387	        cursor: 'pointer',
388	      },
389	
390	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
391	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
392	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
393	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
394	      //
395	      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`

403	        // the other four Fix J sites, whose hidden state only ever applies while a hover-capable
404	        // pointer hasn't revealed the content YET (a state every such pointer can escape), this
405	        // one also applies on a pointer type that can NEVER escape it: `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` never
406	        // matches touch, so there is no reveal path on that pointer type at all (the original,
407	        // Figma-confirmed design — PLP/Wishlist's size picker is a hover-capable-only affordance).
408	        // Keeping this clip-path'd on touch, as Fix J shipped it, left a real `<button>` (each
409	        // `ZimmSizeChip`'s own roving tabindex) permanently in the tab order with no way for that
410	        // pointer type to ever reveal it — reachable by Tab (e.g. a tablet with an external
411	        // keyboard) but invisible and inert forever. Reverted to `display: 'none'` here — the
412	        // hover-capable override, where a reveal genuinely is possible, lives inside
413	        // [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] below instead (see that block's own Fix K note).
414	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
415	          display: 'none',
416	        },
417	      }),
418	      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
419	      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
420	      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
421	      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below). Not part of Fix J's conversion — see
422	      // docblock point 6's own note: this has no reveal counterpart to dead-code, so it correctly
423	      // stays `display: 'none'`.
424	      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
425	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
426	        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
427	        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
428	        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
429	        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
430	        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
431	        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
432	        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
433	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
434	      }),
435	
436	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
437	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
438	          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
439	          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
440	          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
441	          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
442	          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
443	          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
444	          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
445	          // Fix J: was `display: 'none'` — this is the paired hidden state for the two reveal
446	          // rules immediately below and converts along with them (see docblock point 6's own Fix
447	          // J note on why leaving this one as `display: none` would silently dead-code both).
448	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
449	            position: 'absolute',
450	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
451	          },
452	          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
453	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
454	            position: 'static',
455	            clipPath: 'none',
456	          },
457	          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
458	          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
459	          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
460	          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that

463	          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
464	          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`

469	          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
470	          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
471	          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring

473	          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
474	          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
475	          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
476	          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
477	          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
478	          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
479	          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
480	          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
481	          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
482	          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
483	          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
484	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
485	            position: 'static',
486	            clipPath: 'none',
487	          },
488	        }),
489	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
490	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
491	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
492	          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
493	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
494	            position: 'absolute',
495	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
496	          },
497	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
498	          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
499	          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
500	          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
501	          // sticking open after a mouse click.
502	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
503	            position: 'absolute',
504	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
505	          },
506	        }),
507	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
508	          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
509	          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —
510	          // this pointer type genuinely CAN reveal the content below, so it needs to stay in the
511	          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
512	          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display
513	          // (zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts's `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts) — `position`/`clipPath` are
514	          // the only properties the reveal pair below needs to toggle.
515	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
516	            display: 'flex',
517	            position: 'absolute',
518	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
519	          },
520	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
521	          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
522	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
523	            position: 'static',
524	            clipPath: 'none',
525	          },
526	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
527	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
528	            position: 'static',
529	            clipPath: 'none',
530	          },
531	        }),
532	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
533	        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
534	        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
535	        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
536	        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
537	        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/
538	        // `'block'` — converted together, same reasoning as the price/size-selector pair above.
539	        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
540	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
541	            position: 'absolute',
542	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
543	          },
544	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
545	            position: 'static',
546	            clipPath: 'none',
547	          },
548	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
549	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
550	            position: 'static',
551	            clipPath: 'none',
552	          },
553	        }),

558	        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:

564	        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
565	        // Fix J: `display: 'flex'` stays here (unlike the other four sites' reveal rules, which
566	        // drop `display` entirely) — `clipPath: 'none'` is ADDED alongside it, not instead of it.
567	        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
568	        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
569	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
570	        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
571	        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
572	        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
573	        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
574	        //
575	        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
576	        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
577	        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
578	        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
579	        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
580	        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
581	        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
583	          display: 'flex',
584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },
590	        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },
603	
604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
605	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
606	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
607	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
608	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
609	      }),
610	
611	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
612	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
613	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
614	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
615	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
616	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
617	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
618	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
619	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
620	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
621	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
622	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
623	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
624	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
625	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
628	      // that same shape.
629	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
630	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
631	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
632	        }),
633	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
634	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
635	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
636	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
637	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
638	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
639	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
640	          // wrapper's centering.
641	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
642	        }),
643	      },
644	    },
645	  }),
646	};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
   *  docblock point 5. */
  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
 * own by itself:
 *
 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is

        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
          // Fix J: was `display: 'none'` — this is the paired hidden state for the two reveal
          // rules immediately below and converts along with them (see docblock point 6's own Fix
          // J note on why leaving this one as `display: none` would silently dead-code both).
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that
          // focus landing on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers
          // the reveal — mirroring zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own
          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`
          // does not distinguish a real Tab-focused descendant from one that only has focus
          // because the user *clicked* it with a mouse — most browsers give a `<button>` real
          // DOM focus on click, so clicking any interactive control inside the card (an arrow,
          // a size chip, notify-me) left `:focus-within` true, and therefore every reveal below
          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring
          // is warranted, which excludes a mouse-click-focused `<button>` in every evergreen
          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),
        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
          // sticking open after a mouse click.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
        }),
        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —
          // this pointer type genuinely CAN reveal the content below, so it needs to stay in the
          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display
          // (zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts's `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts) — `position`/`clipPath` are
          // the only properties the reveal pair below needs to toggle.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            display: 'flex',
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),
        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/
        // `'block'` — converted together, same reasoning as the price/size-selector pair above.
        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),

        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
        // Fix J: `display: 'flex'` stays here (unlike the other four sites' reveal rules, which
        // drop `display` entirely) — `clipPath: 'none'` is ADDED alongside it, not instead of it.
        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
        //
        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
        },
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'none',
        },
        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
          pointerEvents: 'auto',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'none',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
          pointerEvents: 'auto',
        },
      },

      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
      // that same shape.
      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
        }),
        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
        }),
      },
    },
  }),
};

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.
 */
export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

/**
 * Desktop viewport-width gate shared by the two places with a real min-width-driven layout
 * change: the organism's own PLP bag-icon mobile hide (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) and
 * `ZimmProductCardContent`'s responsive outer padding (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`).
 * Extracted for the identical reason `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above was — each file previously
 * derived this independently from the same `breakpoints.md` token, which is exactly the
 * same-value-typed-twice drift risk a shared constant removes.
 */
export const DESKTOP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`;
